title: Chaining 2-FWL GNNs for Combinatorial Graph Alignment
claim: Candidate alignments are scored by counting matched edges per node, and those scores induce a node ranking used as supervision.
layout: 3 panels: two graphs left, score and ranking boxes right; blue arrows cross
description: A toy worked example with two four-node graphs. Graph G_A has nodes 1–4 in a left column. Graph G_B has nodes a–d in a right column. Curved blue arrows labeled π map 1→c, 2→a, 3→b and 4→d, and they cross in the middle. Edges are drawn as thick arcs beside each column. Green arcs mark edges that match under π: 1-2 with a-c, and 1-3 with b-c. Dark red arcs mark unmatched edges. A gray box at top right lists node scores: score(1)=2, score(2)=1, score(3)=1, score(4)=0. A lavender box below it gives the rankings r^A: [1,2,3,4] and r^B: [c,a,b,d]. The eye goes first to the blue arrows and the green and red edges.
caption: Illustration of Step 2. The permutation $\pi$ maps 1→c, 2→a, 3→b, 4→d. Green edges show matches: edge 1-2 with a-c, and edge 1-3 with b-c. Node 1 has the highest score (2 matched edges), nodes 2 and 3 each have 1 matched edge, and node 4 has no matched edges.
abstract: For the combinatorial graph alignment problem (GAP), finding the node correspondence that maximizes the number of common edges (nce) between two unlabeled graphs, the classical Frank-Wolfe heuristic FAQ remains a strong baseline once it is properly initialized, while existing GNN approaches struggle in the purely structural setting. We introduce a chaining procedure: a sequence of Folklore-type (2-FWL) GNNs in which each network is trained with cross-entropy after decoding the previous network's similarity matrix and ranking nodes by their current alignment quality. This non-differentiable ranking step injects discrete combinatorial feedback at every stage; at inference, we iterate the final network and keep the candidate with highest observed nce. On sparse Erdos-Renyi graphs at noise level 0.25, chained FGNNs used to initialize FAQ reach 85% accuracy versus 13% for FAQ initialized from the convex relaxation, and essentially 0% for prior GNN methods. On correlated regular graphs, where MPNNs with constant features produce identical node embeddings (1-WL fails to refine) and FAQ's convex initialization is degenerate, chaining is the only method among those we evaluate, including Gromov-Wasserstein solvers, that recovers a non-trivial alignment. On three real-world benchmarks (yeast PPI, coauthorship, and road networks), recent comparisons underestimate FAQ by initializing it from a uniform doubly stochastic matrix; initialized from the convex relaxation it already surpasses prior reported numbers, and dataset-specific chained FGNNs further improve on this strengthened baseline. Code and pretrained chains available at: https://github.com/mlelarge/chaining-gnn-graph-alignment.
